In Data Cloud, what is a Data Model Object?
A raw copy of an ingested source table
The canonical, harmonised shape that sources are mapped into
A calculated metric published to Tableau
A permission construct for row-level access
Sources land as Data Lake Objects and are mapped into Data Model Objects, which is where harmonisation and identity resolution happen.
In Data Cloud, where does ingested data land before it is mapped?
A data stream writes into a Data Lake Object in the source’s own shape; mapping then connects it to the Data Model Objects.
What brings data from a source system into Data Cloud?
A data stream connects a source — a Salesforce org, cloud storage, an API — and ingests it on a schedule or in near real time.
What does identity resolution produce in Data Cloud?
Unified profiles from source records that match and reconcile rules say are the same person
A deduplicated copy of the CRM that replaces it
A list of users allowed to log in
Match rules decide which records are the same individual; reconciliation rules decide which value wins. The source records are not changed.
What is a calculated insight in Data Cloud?
A metric defined over the data model, such as lifetime value
An AI-written summary of a record
A data quality score set by an admin
Calculated insights are defined (often in SQL) over unified data — lifetime value, engagement scores — and can be used in segments and activations.
In Data Cloud, what does activating a segment do?
Publishes the audience to a target such as Marketing Cloud or an advertising platform
Turns the segment into a report
Assigns the profiles to a queue
A segment defines an audience; an activation sends it, with chosen attributes, to a destination that will act on it.
In MuleSoft’s API-led connectivity, which layer talks directly to the source system?
System APIs front the source systems. Process APIs orchestrate across them; Experience APIs shape the result for one consumer.
What is the main practical difference between Bulk API 2.0 and Bulk API 1.0?
Bulk API 2.0 supports SOAP as well as REST
Bulk API 2.0 manages batching for you — you upload the whole file
Bulk API 2.0 has no record limit
In 2.0 you create a job, upload the data and Salesforce splits it into batches. In 1.0 you create and manage each batch yourself.
A platform event published with the "Publish Immediately" behaviour is delivered when?
Immediately, whether or not the transaction later rolls back
On the next scheduled batch run
Only to subscribers inside the same org
Publish Immediately delivers even if the transaction rolls back — which is the point when you need an audit signal, and a trap when you assumed the record was saved.
Why does an integration commonly upsert on an External Id field?
It lets the source system key records without knowing Salesforce Ids
It is required for Bulk API
The external system keeps its own key. Upserting on an indexed External Id makes the load idempotent — re-running it updates rather than duplicating.
Large data volumes: what is a skinny table?
A custom object with fewer than ten fields
A Salesforce-created table joining frequently queried fields to avoid a join at read time
An archived copy of deleted records
A Data Cloud data lake object
Salesforce Support creates skinny tables; they contain a subset of fields from the base and custom-field tables so reads avoid the join. They are not self-service.
What does Change Data Capture publish?
Change events for record creates, updates, deletes and undeletes
A nightly CSV of changed records
Change Data Capture streams record changes as events, so an external system stays in sync without polling.
The Pub/Sub API for publishing and subscribing to events is built on what?
Pub/Sub API uses gRPC with Avro-encoded payloads, giving one interface for platform events and change events.
What does the REST API Composite resource let a client do?
Send a series of requests in one call, with later ones using results of earlier ones
Upload files larger than the normal limit
Composite runs up to 25 subrequests in one round trip and can reference an earlier response — create an account, then a contact on it — in a single call.
Why make an Apex callout through a Named Credential?
It holds the endpoint and authentication, so code stores no secrets
It removes the callout governor limit
Named Credentials (with External Credentials) keep the URL and auth in setup; code refers to callout:Name and never handles a password or token.
Without a Named Credential, what must exist before Apex can call an external endpoint?
A Remote Site Setting for it
Callouts to an endpoint not covered by a Named Credential are refused unless a Remote Site Setting allows it.
A SOAP message sent to an endpoint, retried until acknowledged
A REST callout written in Apex
Outbound messages send selected fields as SOAP and retry for up to 24 hours until the endpoint acknowledges. They are configured, not coded.
How does Salesforce Connect show data from an external system?
As external objects, read from the source at the time they are viewed
By copying it into custom objects every night
External objects map to an external data source (for example through OData) and query it live, so the data is never copied into the org.
Up to how many records can the Data Import Wizard load at a time?
50,000 records. Beyond that, Data Loader handles up to five million, and the Bulk API more.
One user owning a very large number of records of one object — guidance says over 10,000
A record owned by a queue
Sharing recalculation and role changes get slow and lock-prone when one owner holds tens of thousands of records — a common result of a single integration user owning everything.
What does marking a custom field as an External ID also do?
External ID fields are indexed, which makes them fast to match on in upserts and selective in queries.
Storing very large volumes of records, such as history or archives, queried through a defined index
Big objects hold billions of records with consistent performance, but queries must follow the object’s index — they are for archive and history, not everyday CRM work.
A lookup field with no value
A very large number of child records pointing at one parent record
Two lookups to the same object
A lookup on a big object
Every child save locks the shared parent, so heavy parallel loads under one parent end in record-lock errors.
Why can a parallel load of many contacts under one account fail with UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW?
Each child insert briefly locks the shared parent account
Bulk API does not support contacts
Group records by parent so one batch holds them, or load serially, to stop batches fighting over the same lock.
What makes a SOQL query selective?
A LIMIT clause on its own
A filter on an indexed field that narrows the result below the selectivity threshold
On large objects the optimizer uses an index only when the filter is selective; otherwise it scans the table.
What does the Query Plan tool in the Developer Console show?
The relative cost of a query and whether it would use an index
It lists candidate plans with their cost, so you can see whether a filter is selective before it runs in production.
How do you get an index on a custom field that is not indexed by default?
Add it to a page layout
Ask Salesforce Support, or make the field an External ID or unique
Support can add custom indexes; External ID and unique fields are indexed automatically.
Why would you run a Bulk API 1.0 load in serial mode?
To reduce lock contention when batches update the same parent records
Because parallel mode is not supported
Serial mode processes one batch at a time — slower, but no two batches compete for the same locks.
How long are high-volume platform event messages kept for replay?
Subscribers that reconnect within three days can replay missed events from a stored ReplayId.
What does an event's ReplayId let a subscriber do?
Resume receiving events from a specific point after a disconnection
A subscriber stores the last ReplayId it processed and asks to continue from there.
What does the "Publish After Commit" behaviour of a platform event mean?
It is delivered before the save
The event is delivered only if the transaction commits
Use it when subscribers must only hear about changes that were actually saved.
What must be done before change events are published for an object?
Select the object for Change Data Capture in Setup
Create a trigger on the object
Enable field history on every field
Only selected objects publish change events; custom channels can group them for particular subscribers.
In a change event, which header field says what kind of change happened?
ChangeEventHeader.changeType is CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE or UNDELETE (or a GAP_ event when details could not be captured).
Which OAuth flow suits a server-to-server integration that has no user present to log in?
The web server flow with a login page
The server signs a JWT with its private key; Salesforce checks it against the certificate on the connected app. The client credentials flow is another option.
What do the OAuth scopes on a connected app control?
What the app's access tokens may be used for
Scopes such as api or refresh_token limit what a token can do; grant only what the integration needs.
Why give an integration its own dedicated user?
Its permissions can be limited to what the integration needs, and its actions can be traced
It can see all data automatically
A named integration user keeps least privilege and makes every change it makes attributable.
Over what period are an org's API request limits counted?
The org's daily API allocation is counted over a rolling 24-hour window; System Overview shows usage.
Which REST API resource runs a SOQL query?
The query resource returns records and a nextRecordsUrl when there are more to fetch.
What does the REST sObject Collections resource allow in one request?
Creating, updating or deleting up to 200 records
Collections cut round trips for small batches; anything larger belongs in the Bulk API.
What does the Salesforce GraphQL API let a client do?
Ask for exactly the fields it needs, across related objects, in one query
One GraphQL request can replace several REST calls and returns no fields the client did not ask for.
How do you expose a custom REST endpoint written in Apex?
Annotate a global class with @RestResource and its methods with @HttpGet, @HttpPost and so on
The endpoint lives under /services/apexrest/ and runs with the calling user's access unless written otherwise.
What does External Services let an admin do?
Register an OpenAPI description of an API and call it from Flow without code
The specification becomes invocable actions; authentication still goes through a Named Credential.
In API-led connectivity, what is an Experience API for?
Talking directly to the source database
Shaping data for one particular consumer, such as a mobile app
Experience APIs sit on top, so a channel gets exactly the shape it needs without changing the layers below.
A catalogue for sharing and discovering APIs and other reusable assets
Teams publish API specifications, connectors and templates there so others reuse rather than rebuild.
MuleSoft's language for transforming data between formats
DataWeave maps JSON, XML, CSV and other formats from one shape to another inside a Mule flow.
Synchronises Salesforce data with a Heroku Postgres database
Apps on Heroku read and write Postgres, and Heroku Connect keeps those tables in step with the org.
What does zero copy (data federation) mean in Data Cloud?
Querying data where it already lives, such as a data warehouse, without copying it in
Federated data stays in the source platform and is queried in place, so nothing has to be kept in sync.
What are data spaces in Data Cloud?
Logical partitions of data, metadata and processes, for example by brand or region
Data spaces let one Data Cloud instance serve several brands while keeping their data apart.
What is the Data Cloud Ingestion API for?
Sending data into Data Cloud from external systems, by streaming or in bulk
Connectors cover common sources; the Ingestion API is for systems that push their own data.
In the Data Cloud data model, which object represents a person?
Source records map to Individual; identity resolution then combines matching individuals into unified profiles.
What do contact point objects, such as Contact Point Email, hold in Data Cloud?
The ways a person can be reached
Email addresses, phone numbers and addresses live in contact point objects linked to the Individual.
"Exact normalised email" is an example of what in Data Cloud?
A match rule used in identity resolution
Match rules decide which source records belong to the same person; reconciliation rules pick the winning values.
What are streaming insights in Data Cloud?
Metrics computed in near real time over streaming data, within a time window
They aggregate events as they arrive — page views in the last ten minutes, say — and can drive data actions.
What does a data action in Data Cloud do?
Sends an event to a target, such as a platform event or a webhook, when its conditions are met
Data actions let a change in Data Cloud start automation elsewhere, for example a flow in the CRM.
What does an upsert with Data Loader need to match existing records?
The record Id or an External ID field
Records that match are updated, the rest are inserted — which is why the External ID must be unique.
What does Hard Delete in Data Loader do?
Deletes records without sending them to the Recycle Bin
Deletes records from production and sandboxes
Hard delete uses the Bulk API and needs the Bulk API Hard Delete permission; the records cannot be undeleted.
How long do deleted records stay in the Recycle Bin?
After 15 days, or when the bin is emptied, records are gone and can no longer be undeleted.
What is a good practice for large data volumes with many old records?
Add more fields to each object
Archive records nobody works on, to keep the working tables small
Smaller tables keep queries selective and sharing recalculations quick; big objects or an external store can keep the history.
How does Apex publish a platform event?
EventBus.publish returns a SaveResult per event; whether delivery waits for commit depends on the event's publish behaviour.
How does Apex refer to a Named Credential in a callout?
req.setEndpoint('callout:My_Service/path') — the platform adds the base URL and the authentication.
